reasoning prefixes from retrieved (but different) examples creates misleading procedural noise.

different-but-similar queries. Also consumes significant token budget.

| symmetric_confusion_memory | 26.7% | 40.0% | 90.0% | 52.2% (+0.0) |

Tied the frontier exactly — no regression, no improvement.

The reverse edges did fire much more frequently (confirmed in prototype traces). However, the
disambiguation phase filling extra slots for confusion partners displaced similar examples that
were already doing useful work. The net effect cancelled out: more disambiguation fires, but the
examples injected via disambiguation were not meaningfully better than what similarity retrieval

ground truths are stored and tracked as atomic strings, so confusion lookup operates on composite
keys that rarely match individual label predictions. Future candidates should either decompose
multi-label targets into individual-label confusion tracking, or explore entirely different
selection axes (e.g. label coverage maximization, temporal weighting).

**Step 1 analysis complete.** Now prototyping the two candidates before implementing.

**Hypothesis 1 (Exploitation, Axis E):** The confusion matrix in all prior systems stores composite multi-label ground truths as atomic strings (e.g., "诈骗;信用卡诈骗"). This means when pred="诈骗" and gt="诈骗;信用卡诈骗", the pair pred→gt is stored as an unresolvable key. At disambiguation time, looking up "诈骗" finds nothing because the key only exists as the full composite string. Decomposing labels at learn time — recording "诈骗"→"信用卡诈骗" individually — should make the confusion matrix fire on the far more common single-label predictions.

**Hypothesis 2 (Exploration, Axis C):** After identifying the most similar example's label as the "top candidate", actively select cross-label boundary examples — examples that are similar to the query but belong to a different label — and place them first in context. This forces the model to see near-misses before confirming the top candidate, sharpening the decision boundary. Unlike `contrastive_boundary_memory` (iter 11) which used the confusion matrix and "[NOT: label]" annotation, this uses purely query-time cross-label similarity with no annotation change.
